author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: God and Groypers: The Christo-Fascist Conference in Texas
content:
Irving, TX – White supremacist Nicholas J. Fuentes walked on stage of the Irving Convention Center just outside of Dallas to roaring applause and chants. One young attendee shot up from his seat and exuberantly began clapping his hands above his head.




Behind Fuentes was a WWE-like promo video where the streamer shouts that he will “die for America” while a cross flashes in the center of the screen and a battleship fires munitions at an unknown target.




At the podium, a smirk crept across his face as the audience broke out into “USA” chants.




“Yes,” he said, nodding his head and basking in the zealotry before him.







Nick Fuentes on stage at the Christ is King conference. Source: NXR Live stream.







This was the third and final day of the “Christ is King: America after Trump” conference in Irving, a diverse suburb of Dallas, Texas. Until moments before he was welcomed on the stage, Fuentes was an unannounced mystery speaker intended to cap off the Christo-fascist jubilee.




Roughly 1,000 people showed up from around the country to attend the convention, put on by Pastor Joel Webbon’s New Christian Right, or NXR, an explicitly Christian nationalist organization that aligns more with Fuentes’ groypers than the MAGA coalition that holds power in the Republican Party. Righteous 39

title: From Hospitals to Palantir HQ: Protests Across England Over Controversial Healthcare Data Deal
content:
London, England — “We need to take our power back! Our UK government needs to represent the interests of the British public, who elected them into power, not the Zionist entity,” said Taby Khan, a health research scientist protesting outside The Royal London Hospital.




On October 1, doctors, nurses, health care workers and members of the public took to the streets at more than 40 locations across England, demanding an end to the controversial £330 million ($442 million) contract between the National Health Service (NHS) and U.S. technology company Palantir. 




The mobilization was organized by the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Health Workers for a Free Palestine, Amnesty International, Medact, Keep Our NHS Public, and other groups. They argue that a company known for its work with military and immigration agencies, including the development of AI and surveillance technologies, should not have access to the sensitive health data of 

60 million people

 in England.













The protests began outside hospitals across the country, including four locations in London, before culminating in a demonstration outside Palantir’s London headquarters.

title: James O’Keefe and Cam Higby Evade Press and Protesters After Hearing, Cancel Presser
content:

The two men, surrounded by a security detail led by former Minneapolis Policeman Bob Kroll, rushed into the building without speaking a word while press and protesters surrounded them.







Cam Higby (left) and James O’Keefe (To the right of Higby) waving at press, supporters and protesters, following their arraignment on Nov. 16.

The “mob” was ultimately the excuse for not conducting a press conference outside of the building, for which cameras and microphones had been set up well in advance. Instead, the two slinked out the back while other high-profile supporters took the opportunity to leave.

title: Two Palestine Solidarity Activists Refuse to Testify Before a Grand Jury
content:

The structure houses Elbit Systems of America, the domestic branch of an Israeli weapons manufacturer that’s a key supplier of drones and ground equipment used in the country’s ongoing 

genocide in Palestine

The two were participating in an action organized by Palestine Action U.S. Some blockaded the road leading to the facility while Shergalis and Ross, along with others, continued to the building.




A few protesters stayed on the ground and sprayed the facade with red paint, sealed doors shut with a bike lock, and broke windows. Shergalis and Ross made their ways to the building’s roof and lit flares to announce their presence while attempting to damage the building’s HVAC system.




Both women were arrested that day, along with Calla Walsh. Paige Belanger, another participant, was arrested days later. All four were

author: By Sophia Potsi, Contributor
title: Europe’s Broken Promise: From Open Camps to High-Tech Prisons
content:
Greek Islands – In 2015, the Greek island of Lesvos was the epicenter of the so-called migration crisis. With arrivals reaching 2,000 people per day, images from the island reflected the solidarity of the locals. Fishermen were seen pulling people out of the water and elderly women took care of newborns in village squares. The islanders’ response of solidarity with people fleeing war was so remarkable that they were nominated for a Nobel Peace Prize.




For a while, Lesvos was a place that functioned as an in-between, an island that people stayed for a little bit and then left to continue their journey to Europe. But after the EU-Turkey deal in 2016, the islands were turned from places that people passed to places that people were held. From passageways they became waiting rooms in closed camps on the edge of Europe. 




And this is how Moria was built, the camp that in the following years would become a symbol of Europe’s brutal containment and inhumane policies and treatment against refugees, migrants, and people on the move.




Moria: Suffering and Resilience




Moria camp, formally known as the Moria Reception and Identification Center, was the largest refugee camp in Europe. It was originally built to hold 3,000 people, and had help up to 20,000 people at peak times before it burned down in 2020. 




The conditions in the camp were horrible. There was no running water

title: ICE Agent Falsely Accused Federal Defender of Helping Client Evade Arrest and Deportation
content:
Minneapolis, MN — It was supposed to be another routine court appearance.




Assistant Federal Defender Michael Deates and his Salvadoran client settled inside the Minneapolis courtroom on April 28. ICE Deportation Officer Michael O’Neal sat inside the gallery when he heard a familiar name: Ezequiel Portillo-Rodriguez.




He pulled out his government phone and then searched for the name. A Certificate of Nonexistence (CTNE) that he filed in April 2025 popped up. To O’Neal, this meant that there were no official records of Portillo-Rodriguez ever holding a visa, green card or U.S. citizenship. He texted agent Blake Willwerscheid, asking if he knew about the case. Willwersheid told him that Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Special Agent Brubaker was in charge of the case. A prosecutor later testified that this HSI Agent thought he was talking to an agent Witt in St. Paul.




Had O’Neal looked through court records he would have found something more relevant than a CTNE. On Sept. 2, 2025, Portillo-Rodriguez started his six-month stint inside the notorious Golden State Annex in McFarland, Ca. He filed an asylum claim while inside the private immigration jail run by GEO Group. title: Twin Cities Demand Justice For Kohen Wiley Killing
content:
St. Paul, MN – When one-year-old Kohen Wiley was shot by police in Mississippi this summer, residents in the Twin Cities felt the pain of a life lost to police violence. In late October, when the body-worn camera footage of the shooting was released and the officer’s use of force ruled justified, they knew they needed to respond.




So on Oct. 25, local Black women, many of whom have experienced losing a loved one to police violence themselves, rallied residents to show up and march in hopes of raising awareness and demanding accountability for the one-year-old infant shot by police in June.




The march was spurred by the Mississippi Attorney General ruling that the officer who fired the shots that killed Wiley and struck another woman in the car, was justified in using deadly force. Protests have taken place across the country, including last month’s march in St. Paul.




On October 25, a crowd gathered in front of the Governor’s mansion where speakers addressed attendees. Though Wiley was killed in Mississippi, organizers saw a direct connection to his killing and the many police shootings that have burdened their community.




“When a murder happens to any one of us, it happens to all of us,” Toshira Garraway Allen, founder of 

Families Supporting Families Against Police Violence

, told the crowd.

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: Hennepin County Surveilled Anti-HERC Activists Since 2023
content:
Minneapolis, MN — A report released by the Zero Burn Coalition documents years of surveillance conducted against activists pushing for clean air in Minneapolis. The revelations came from documents that the organization obtained through public information requests.




At the center of this is the Hennepin Energy Recovery Center (HERC), a nearly 40-year-old trash incinerator neighboring Target Field in Minneapolis permitted to burn 365,000 tons of garbage annually. Activists, including those with the Zero Burn Coalition, have advocated for its closure for years, citing the amount of pollution it produces and the disproportionate effect on marginalized communities.




A short walk to the west of the facility is historically Black and working-class neighborhoods of North Minneapolis, which bear the brunt of the plant’s pollution. 




Coinciding with the release of the report on Oct. 22, community members and Minnesota Environmental Justice Table (MNEJT) activists and leaders convened along Olson Memorial Highway in the Heritage Park neighborhood for a press conference, in full view of HERC’s foreboding smoke stacks on the other side of Interstate 94.

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: Hennepin County Charges Far-Right Influencers Following Election Fraud Stunt
content:
Minneapolis, MN – Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty 

announced

 felony charges of identity theft and unlawful voting against far-right influencers James O’Keefe and Cam Higby 

on Wednesday

, Oct. 28.




“Before the August 11 primary election this office was very clear that reports of unlawful activity related to the election would be investigated and charged if appropriate,” Moriarty said during a press conference held on Oct. 27.




The charges stem from a series of videos produced by the duo during the Minnesota primary election on Aug. 11, where the two attempted to document what they alleged was a flaw in the state’s voter registration system that allows voters to prove their residence by having neighbors vouch for them. 




In the videos, Higby and O’Keefe, representing O’Keefe’s Florida-based Citizens Justice League, provide the names of actual voters in the area to poll workers but stop short of signing the oath to receive the ballot.




“Minnesota law states clearly that no individual shall intentionally misrepresent their identity in applying for a ballot,” Moriarty said, addressing the fact that neither man actually received a ballot. “The charges filed today are appropriate to address the conduct of Mr. O’Keefe and Mr. Higby.”

Rouvikonas

criminal organization

another

author: By Dan Feidt, Unicorn Riot
title: ‘Icepick’ Leak Exposes Thousands of Homeland Security Personnel, Groups and More
content:
Washington, DC — There’s been yet another major security breach among federal agencies. The Department of Homeland Security’s ‘single sign-on’ (SSO) login system was reportedly subverted by a hacker going by “Department of Peace” (DoP), which has revealed thousands upon thousands of federal employee records. Around one-fifth of Homeland Security’s personnel have been exposed. Offices and locations are identified in great detail, from Canadian airports to agents in U.S. embassies around the world. Groups assigned within the SSO system, going back at least to 2011, are also exposed, showing the names of globe-spanning activities, and management personnel handling undercover operations.




Thousands of personnel records include supervisors and subordinates, which enabled generating gigantic organizational charts automatically across these agencies. Combine this with the groups (some officials tagged in dozens) and one can easily browse around the highest levels of activities, including thousands of groups dealing with surveillance, special operations, finance, social media, and much, much more. updates are at the end of this post
